headline: Revenue and profit surge as cloud storage demand accelerates

drivers.explanation: CEO Dave Mosley attributed the quarter's revenue strength to robust cloud data-center demand for mass-capacity storage and disciplined execution; no unit-volume or pricing breakdown was given.
GAAP gross margin expanded to 52.3% from 37.4% a year ago; the release attributes this to the same cloud/exabyte demand strength cited for revenue rather than a separate cost driver.
Net income growth (+165% y/y) lagged pre-tax income growth (+206% y/y) because the effective tax rate normalized to ~14% this quarter from an unusually low ~0.8% a year ago.
EPS growth (+149% y/y) lagged net income growth (+165% y/y) due to a higher diluted share count (232M vs 218M a year ago).

Mosley cited FY2026 as a record-profitability year (34% annual revenue growth, $3.1B free cash flow) driven by cloud demand and the Mozaic/HAMR product roadmap, with momentum expected to continue into FY2027.

summary_short: Seagate's fiscal Q4 2026 revenue rose 48.5% y/y to $3,629M and GAAP diluted EPS climbed to $5.58 (+149.1% y/y) on robust cloud data-center demand, and the company guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue to $4.1B ± $100M and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $7.30 ± $0.20.
summary_long: GAAP diluted EPS of $5.58 (+149.1% y/y) reflected a 48.5% y/y revenue jump to $3,629M on cloud data-center demand for mass-capacity storage, per CEO Dave Mosley. GAAP gross margin expanded to 52.3% from 37.4% a year ago. The company generated $1,118M of free cash flow this quarter, retired $302M of debt, and returned $283M to shareholders via dividends and buybacks; cash rose to $1,704M and long-term debt fell to $3,380M. Seagate guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue to $4.1B ± $100M and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $7.30 ± $0.20, citing continued cloud momentum and minimal expected tariff/geopolitical impact.
